title: Affine smooth model in a noetherian approximation
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], N a noetherian approximation [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], and i a stage. Let p : Y → N.D(i) be locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Suppose f : X → S is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and a : X → Y makes (a, f, p, N.π(i)) a cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is an object j of Over i for which the canonical second projection Y ×_{N.D(i)} N.D(j.left) → N.D(j.left) is smooth.

source.place: Tag 0C0C, limits.tex, lemma-descend-smooth, with Situation 081D; affine descent via Tag 0CAQ and comparison via Tag 01ZM(2)-(3)

proof.text: Apply exists_smooth_stage_of_affine_limit to N.D, N.π and N.isLimit. The affine-transition and Noetherian hypotheses are N.isAffineHom_map and N.isNoetherian_obj, and Noetherian schemes are quasi-separated. This is exactly the official exists_smooth_affine_model proof. The former existential model follows by taking Z to be this canonical pullback, q its second projection and the identity comparison; its finiteness properties are preserved by base change.

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.NoetherianApproximation.exists_smooth_affine_model
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (N : S.NoetherianApproximation) {i : N.I}
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (p : Y ⟶ N.D.obj i)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
    (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] (a : X ⟶ Y)
    (H : IsPullback a f p (N.π.app i)) :
    ∃ j : Over i, Smooth (pullback.snd p (N.D.map j.hom))

statement_change.old_statement: For the data of the eventual smoothness theorem, there are a later stage j, a scheme Z and a finitely presented quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism q : Z → D(j.left), with q smooth, together with an isomorphism from Z to the pullback of p.

The official stronger statement implies the old one by the canonical pullback and the identity comparison. There are no current DAG citers or Lean consumers of the retired copy.

old_proof.text: Apply the existing affine-limit smooth-stage theorem to the Noetherian approximation diagram; its hypotheses are supplied by the approximation fields. Take the resulting pullback as Z, with q the pullback projection; pullback preserves finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, and the comparison isomorphism is reflexivity.
